report_name: Microsoft details AI-assisted invoice fraud impersonating CEOs

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Attackers conducted a large-scale business email compromise (BEC) campaign, sending over a million fraudulent emails to trick employees into making urgent payments.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
attack_patterns.description: The attackers registered domains that were visually similar to the target company's domain (typosquatting) to send the initial fraudulent emails.

attack_patterns.name: Impersonation
attack_patterns.description: The campaign impersonated Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) to pressure accounts payable personnel. The attackers also included forged email conversation threads to lend legitimacy to the fraudulent requests.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing via Social Engineering LLM
attack_patterns.description: Generative AI was used to create highly convincing and tailored email content, including email templates and supporting documents, to automate and scale the personalized BEC attacks.

tools.name: Generative AI
tools.description: Used by attackers to generate highly convincing and tailored email content, including email templates, forged invoices, and fabricated email chains to conduct invoice fraud at scale.

campaigns.name: AI-Assisted BEC Invoice Fraud Campaign
campaigns.description: A large-scale, sophisticated business email compromise (BEC) campaign between August 3-5, 2026, that utilized generative AI to impersonate CEOs and conduct invoice fraud against US companies. The campaign sent over one million emails in three days.
campaigns.objective: Trick employees into making fraudulent Automated Clearing House (ACH) payments.

identities.name: IT services companies
identities.description: A class of organizations in the IT services sector targeted by the AI-assisted BEC campaign.

identities.name: Real estate companies
identities.description: A class of organizations in the real estate sector targeted by the AI-assisted BEC campaign.

identities.name: Manufacturing companies
identities.description: A class of organizations in the manufacturing sector targeted by the AI-assisted BEC campaign.

infrastructure.name: Typosquatted Domains
infrastructure.description: Look-alike domains, visually similar to the target company's domain, were registered and used to send fraudulent emails.

infrastructure.name: Trusted Email Delivery Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Attackers used trusted email delivery services to help their fraudulent emails bypass standard anti-spam and anti-phishing controls.

indicators.name: Potential BEC with Mismatched Reply-To Headers
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential BEC with Mismatched From and Reply-To Headers
id: f1a2b3c4-d5e6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: >-
  Detects a potential Business Email Compromise (BEC) email where the 'From' header contains an internal domain but a 'Reply-To' header is also present.
  This is a common tactic to redirect replies to an attacker. Further analysis is required to confirm the Reply-To is external and not legitimate (e.g., a mailing list).
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/10/protecting-organizations-ai-assisted-executive-impersonation-invoice-fraud/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-13
tags:
  - attack.t1566
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: email
detection:
  selection:
    Keywords|all:
      - 'From: '
      - '@yourcompany.com' # Placeholder, replace with your internal domain
      - 'Reply-To: '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects emails where the 'From' address appears legitimate but the 'Reply-To:' address is different, a common BEC tactic.

indicators.name: Potential AI-Assisted BEC Invoice Fraud Keywords
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential AI-Assisted BEC Invoice Fraud Keywords
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects keywords associated with an AI-assisted BEC campaign focused on urgent invoice fraud for ServiceNow renewals.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/10/protecting-organizations-ai-assisted-executive-impersonation-invoice-fraud/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-13
tags:
  - attack.t1566
  - attack.initial_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: email
detection:
  selection:
    Keywords|all:
      - 'Urgent ACH Payment'
      - 'ServiceNow Renewal'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects keywords such as 'Urgent ACH Payment' and 'ServiceNow Renewal' in email subjects or bodies, which were used in the AI-assisted BEC campaign.
